cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7), and he just told them love is the fulfillment of the law (Romans 13:10). Now he gets practical with believers who don't all see things the same way. First up is the one whose faith is weak, and Paul says accept him.

cards.question: Paul says to accept the believer whose faith is weak. How should they do it?

answers.text: Without passing judgment on his opinions
Only once his faith grows stronger

cards.text: Paul gives an example: one person has faith to eat all things, and another eats only vegetables. Me, I've got faith to eat all COOKIES, and friend, that's not a gift, that's a problem.

cards.question: True or false: Paul calls the one who eats all things weak.

cards.text: Paul has a word for both sides: the one who eats everything must not belittle the one who doesn't, and the one who doesn't must not judge the one who does. NOBODY gets to walk out of this verse with their nose in the air.

cards.question: Paul says the one who doesn't eat everything must not judge the one who does, for God has ___ him.

cards.text: Then Paul asks, “Who are you to judge someone else’s servant?” Picture strolling into somebody else's bakery and grading their cookies while the owner is standing RIGHT THERE.

cards.question: Paul pictures that believer as someone else's servant. Who does Paul say that servant stands or falls to?
True or false: Paul says that servant will fall unless the church holds him up.

cards.text: Now Paul switches from food to the calendar: one person regards a certain day above the others, and someone else considers every day alike. Me, I regard Cookie Day above the others, and around here that's every day.

cards.question: About special days, Paul says each one should be fully ___ in his own mind.

cards.text: Paul looks at all of them: the one who keeps a special day, the one who eats, and the one who abstains. Three different choices, and you'd think he's about to call one of them out.

cards.question: Paul says the one who keeps a special day, the one who eats and the one who abstains all have one thing in common. What is it?

answers.text: They do it to the Lord
They do it to please others
They do it to earn God's favor

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the one who eats gives thanks to God, and the one who abstains gives thanks to God too.

cards.text: Then Paul zooms way out: none of us lives to himself alone, and none of us dies to himself alone. I tried living to myself alone once, friend, it was called the junk drawer, and I do NOT recommend it.

cards.question: Paul says whether we live or die, we ___ to the Lord.
Paul says Christ died and returned to life for a reason. What is it?

answers.text: To be Lord of both the dead and the living
To settle every argument about food
To make every day exactly alike

cards.question: Paul asks why anyone would judge or belittle a brother. What reason does he give to stop?

answers.text: We will all stand before God's judgment seat
The church leaders will sort it all out
Our brothers will only judge us back

cards.text: Paul backs it up with what is written: “As surely as I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow before Me; every tongue will confess to God.” Every knee, friend, and nobody's sitting this one out.

cards.question: Paul sums it up: each of us will give an account of ___ to God.

cards.text: So Paul says, “Therefore let us stop judging one another.” And instead of judging, he tells them to make up their minds about something else.

cards.question: Instead of judging one another, what does Paul tell them to make up their minds about?

answers.text: Not to put a stumbling block in a brother's way
Not to share a meal with a weaker brother
Not to bring up special days ever again

cards.text: A stumbling block is like leaving the mixer cord stretched across the kitchen floor. YOU know it's there, but whoever comes around that corner next is going DOWN.
Then Paul says, “I am convinced and fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself.” But he's got a twist for the person who sees it differently.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says if anyone regards something as unclean, then for him it is unclean.

cards.text: Now picture it: you're eating something, and your brother is distressed by what you eat. You're fine, he's not, and now Paul has something to say about YOU.

cards.question: If your brother is distressed by what you eat, what does Paul say you're no longer doing?
Paul says don't destroy your brother by your eating, because he's the brother for whom ___ died.

cards.text: Paul adds: don't let what you consider good get spoken of as evil. A cookie can be PERFECT, but if you serve it by throwing it at people, that's all anybody's gonna remember.

cards.question: Paul says the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, ___, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

cards.text: Paul says whoever serves Christ this way is pleasing to God and approved by men. Pleasing to God AND people? Friend, I've had batches that couldn't even please ME.

cards.question: So then, what does Paul tell the believers to pursue?

answers.text: What leads to peace and builds each other up
Whatever proves which side is right
Strict rules for every meal they share

cards.text: Paul says, “Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food.” Over FOOD, friend, and I've wanted the last cookie in the box real bad, but never THAT bad.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says all food is clean, so it doesn't matter if your eating makes someone stumble.
Paul names things it's better not to do if they would cause a brother to stumble. Which ones?

cards.text: Paul says keep your belief about such matters between yourself and God. Not everything needs to go in the group chat, friend.

cards.question: Paul says blessed is the one who does not ___ himself by what he approves.

cards.text: Paul's last word is for the one who has doubts about eating something. He's not sure, but he eats it anyway.

cards.question: Why does Paul say the one who has doubts is condemned if he eats?

answers.text: His eating is not from faith
The food is unclean in itself

cards.question: True or false: Paul ends by saying everything that is not from faith is sin.

findings.problem: Stop 1's choice cards follow a fixed rotation. Cards 2, 4, 6, 8, 9, 11, 13, 14 and 16 run multiple choice, true or false, fill in the blank, three times in a row.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: The question begins "Paul pictures that believer". "That believer" points back to story card 7, which is no longer on screen, so the baker has to remember which believer is meant.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The statement "Paul says that servant will fall..." depends on card 8's question. "That servant" points back to a card the baker can no longer see.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The joke "I tried living to myself alone once... it was called the junk drawer" changes the backstory in two ways. In the backstory he didn't choose the drawer, and he wasn't alone there: "Every one of them was waiting. They were all in it together," and he welcomed every newcomer.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The joke treats "lives to himself alone" as living alone, cut off from others. In Romans 14:7-8 it means living for oneself rather than to the Lord. The comparison doesn't match the verse's core action, and it muddies what the verse means.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "To settle every argument about food" and "To make every day exactly alike" are not believable reasons for Christ's death and return to life. They come across as throwaways, so the Bible-sounding right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card tells no part of the passage. It only explains "stumbling block" with a joke about a mixer cord and repeats verse 13, which cards 1 and 2 already covered.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card spends its words explaining what a stumbling block is. A hard word belongs in a dictionary pop-up, not on a card.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: Stop 1 card 1 told the baker that love is the fulfillment of the law (Romans 13:10). With that in mind, a baker could argue that someone no longer acting in love is no longer "Keeping the law", so that wrong answer is too close to the right one.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: No story card sets up verse 17. The blank asks the baker to guess the second word in the list "righteousness, ___, and joy", which is wording they haven't seen. This is the same as the Psalm 23 "paths of…" bad example.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Nothing before this card introduces condemning oneself, so "condemn", "praise" and "forgive" all fit the line. The baker can only guess the verse's wording, not reason it out.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
